headline_marked: Ronaldo, Ramos fire [[Portugal past Croatia into last 16]]
headline: Ronaldo, Ramos fire Portugal past Croatia into last 16
summary: Cristiano Ronaldo broke his World Cup knockout duck with a penalty, while a late strike from Ramos secured the 2-1 victory in Toronto.
details: Portugal advanced to the World Cup last 16 after defeating Croatia 2-1 in a dramatic Round of 32 clash in Toronto. Cristiano Ronaldo converted a 68th-minute penalty to level the score at 1-1, while Sergio Ramos provided the winning goal in stoppage time.
Croatia had initially taken the lead in the second half through Ivan Perisic. However, Ronaldo's equalizer breathed new life into the Portugal campaign, leading to the eventual victory.
The match was an emotional occasion, coinciding with the first death anniversary of Portugal and Liverpool forward Diogo Jota.

Ronaldo made history by becoming the oldest outfield player to start a World Cup knockout match at 41 years and 147 days. He also moved into sole possession of second place on the all-time list for World Cup appearances with his 26th match.
Croatia captain Luka Modric also set a record as the second-oldest outfield player to start a knockout game at 40 years and 296 days. Both players surpassed the previous record held by Edin Dzeko.
Ronaldo has now become the first player to score in six different World Cup editions and is Portugal's outright leading scorer in the tournament with 10 goals.
Portugal will now face Spain in Dallas for a place in the quarter-finals.

Portugal advanced to the World Cup last 16 after defeating Croatia 2-1 in a dramatic Round of 32 clash in Toronto. Cristiano Ronaldo converted a 68th-minute penalty to level the score at 1-1, while Sergio Ramos provided the winning goal in stoppage time.

Croatia had initially taken the lead in the second half through Ivan Perisic. However, Ronaldo's equalizer breathed new life into the Portugal campaign, leading to the eventual victory.

The match was an emotional occasion, coinciding with the first death anniversary of Portugal and Liverpool forward Diogo Jota.

Ronaldo made history by becoming the oldest outfield player to start a World Cup knockout match at 41 years and 147 days. He also moved into sole possession of second place on the all-time list for World Cup appearances with his 26th match.

Croatia captain Luka Modric also set a record as the second-oldest outfield player to start a knockout game at 40 years and 296 days. Both players surpassed the previous record held by Edin Dzeko.

Ronaldo has now become the first player to score in six different World Cup editions and is Portugal's outright leading scorer in the tournament with 10 goals.

Portugal will now face Spain in Dallas for a place in the quarter-finals.

headline_marked: [[Broiler chicken prices jump BDT 20/kg]] in 3-4 days; potatoes, chili, eggplant also up
headline: Broiler chicken prices jump BDT 20/kg in 3-4 days; potatoes, chili, eggplant also up
summary: Retail markets in Dhaka see significant price hikes for broiler and Sonali chicken, potatoes, eggplant, and green chilies, driven by supply shortages from farms and recent rainfall.
details: The retail prices of broiler and Sonali chicken have increased by BDT 20 per kilogram within just three to four days. Alongside poultry, prices for potatoes, eggplant, and green chilies have also risen across various markets.

Earlier this week, broiler chicken was sold at BDT 170-180 per kg, but it is now BDT 190-200 per kg in Dhaka markets. Sonali chicken prices also saw a BDT 20 increase, now ranging from BDT 300-350 per kg, up from BDT 280-330 last week.

According to Sohail Ahmed, a chicken seller at Karwan Bazar, the primary reason for the broiler chicken price hike is increased costs at farm and wholesale levels. He noted that power outages in various areas prevented many farms from raising new broiler chickens due to intense heat.
Additionally, some farmers sold their chickens prematurely to avoid losses, leading to a supply shortage that has driven up prices. This disruption in the supply chain directly impacts retail costs.

Potato prices have also climbed, with a 22% increase over the last month, now selling at BDT 25-30 per kg, up from BDT 20-25. Data from the Trading Corporation of Bangladesh (TCB) indicates a 15% rise in domestic garlic prices, now BDT 90-140 per kg from BDT 60-140 a month ago.

Narrow rice varieties like Nazirshail and Miniket have seen a BDT 2 increase per kg, now BDT 72-85. Medium rice types such as Paijam and BRRI-28 are up BDT 2-3 per kg, while coarse rice increased by BDT 1-2 per kg.

The most significant rice price hike was for Chinigura or Polao rice, which surged by BDT 15 per kg in the last month, now selling at BDT 160-170 per kg. These increases affect staple food items across the board.
Green chili and eggplant prices have also risen within a week. Green chilies are now BDT 120-160 per kg, and eggplant is BDT 70-100 per kg, both up BDT 20 per kg from last week’s prices.

Abbas Akond, a vegetable seller at Mohammadpur Krishi Market, attributed the increase in chili and eggplant prices to reduced supply caused by several days of rain this week. He expects prices to return to normal once the supply stabilizes.
